page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 dedicated vCPUs spanning 4 physical cores on an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor based on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration supplies 32 GB of system memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4 GB per virtual core. Storage is provisioned via an integrated 402 GB local NVMe SSD, and the configuration includes zero discrete GPUs. Supported instruction sets include AVX-512 extensions (with VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic primitives such as AES and SHA-NI.

Benchmark data demonstrates strong single-core compute performance, placing in the top 25% under stress-ng evaluation alongside strong Geekbench text processing scores. PassMark CPU execution and Geekbench multi-core results consistently align with the middle 50% performance bracket. A clear technical tradeoff exists in large-block uncached memory bandwidth, which measures in the lower percentiles for both reads and writes. Cached operations remain standard, but applications requiring sustained large memory write streams will encounter memory throughput limits.

Because high-speed NVMe storage is bundled directly with dedicated CPU resources, the instance provides efficient localized data processing without requiring external network storage attachments. Workload profiles matching this specification include web serving, relational database instances, caching tiers such as Redis, software compilation, and CI/CD automation pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-8-lssd is a general-purpose cloud instance configured with 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor, 32 GB of memory, and a bundled 402 GB local NVMe SSD. Operating on the x86_64 architecture, the processor provides vector and matrix extensions including AVX-512 and cryptographic instructions. Benchmark evaluations show top-quartile single-core CPU capabilities and solid text processing metrics, accompanied by median multi-threaded execution and static web serving throughput. A primary architectural limitation lies in large-block uncached memory bandwidth, which ranks among the lower quartiles for sequential read and write streams. With a balanced 4 GB of memory per core and high-speed local disk storage, this instance matches relational database workloads, caching layers, software compilation tasks, and general web applications requiring fast scratch storage.
